From: Angela Park <angela.park@finvest.com>

Cc: David Lo <david.lo@finvest.com>

Subject: SIG questionnaire — clarification on backup encryption and key custody

Hi Rachel,

We're working through the SIG you sent and have two items that are ambiguous in the way they map to our environment. We want to make sure our auditors and cloud team interpret your responses the same way we do before we lock them into our procurement bundle. The two questions: Q12 (Encryption of data at rest: backups/snapshots) and Q27 (Key management — who controls CMKs used for persistent backups and snapshot exports).

The SIG wording is short and seems to conflate provider-encrypted snapshots with application-level encrypted backups. Specifically:
- Does Redwood's hosted offering use customer-managed keys (CMK) for snapshot-level backups by default, or are snapshots encrypted with a provider-managed key with Redwood retaining key custody?
- For Dedicated / Private deployments, can customers require their own KMS that controls both runtime encryption and persisted backups/snapshots?

Could we schedule a quick call to talk through the intended answers and have Redwood provide concise phrasing we can include in our vendor risk spreadsheet? If you have a short written interpretation that maps each SIG question to a one-sentence answer, that would help a lot.

Thanks,

Angela Park
Security Engineer — FinVest
security@finvest.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Angela Park <angela.park@finvest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:18:45 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — clarification on backup encryption and key custody

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear note. Happy to sync.

Quick answers up-front so you can move forward before our call:
- Hosted API (default): snapshots and provider-level backups are encrypted using the cloud provider-managed KMS; Redwood does not expose CMKs to customers in the hosted tier — Redwood manages the provider CMK and access.
- Dedicated: customers can opt to attach a customer-managed KMS (CMK) for both runtime and persisted snapshot encryption; key policies must allow Redwood service principals to use the CMK for cryptographic operations required by the runtime.
- Private/on-prem: customer fully controls keys and rotation; Redwood's on-prem package supports integration with customer KMS/HSM.

I've attached a short draft (sig-response-draft.pdf) that maps Q12 and Q27 to one-sentence responses and callouts for evidence. Can we do a 30m call Monday to confirm?

Proposed times:
- Mon 11/23 09:00-09:30 PT
- Mon 11/23 12:00-12:30 PT

If those don't work, happy to shift. CC'ing Neha from Security (ownership for evidence) and Marissa from Sales (procurement coordinator).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:02 -08:00
Subject: Meeting notes: FinVest SIG call (Q12/Q27) — 11/23/2026

Notes from today's 30m sync with Angela and David (FinVest):

Attendees: Angela Park (FinVest), David Lo (FinVest), Rachel Kim (Redwood), Neha Kapoor (Redwood), Marissa Cole (Redwood)

Summary of agreements:
- Hosted (Redwood-managed) snapshots: encrypted with the provider-managed KMS by default. Redwood holds operational control over those provider keys for hosted customers (we do not provision or surface CMKs to hosted customers). This matches the short answer Rachel provided in email.

- Dedicated: customers can configure a customer-managed KMS (CMK) for both live encryption and persisted snapshots/backups. When CMK is used, the customer owns the key material; Redwood requires an allowlist policy that grants the Redwood service principal permission to Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey operations as needed. We agreed to provide an example key policy snippet as evidence.

- Private/on-prem: full customer key custody. For air-gapped on-prem installs, Redwood will document KMS integration points and will not maintain key material.

Edge cases / clarifications:
- Cross-region replication: when snapshots are replicated between regions, encryption remains in-place. If customer-supplied CMKs are used, cross-region replication requires either a multi-region CMK or replication using encrypted blobs under provider controls (we documented the options).
- Backups exported for restores: exported snapshot artifacts are encrypted with the same key used for storage; if CMK is customer-managed, the exported object remains encrypted under that CMK.
- Rotation: CMK rotation policy is customer-controlled; Redwood supports key rotation without decrypting persisted blobs when the provider supports envelope encryption and rewrapping.

Requested evidence items (FinVest):
1) Example KMS key policy JSON that includes Redwood service principal allowlist (we agreed to redact account IDs).
2) Screenshot of Dedicated control plane KMS configuration UI (or a configuration file for Private).
3) SOC 2 Type II attestation (latest) — provided by Redwood as an evidence packet.
4) One-sentence Q12/Q27 phrasing to paste into FinVest vendor risk tool.

Action items + owners + ETA:
- Neha: produce key policy snippet (redacted) and Dedicated config screenshot — ETA 2 business days (by 11/25).
- Rachel: push finalized one-sentence answers into the SIG PDF and include SOC 2 PDF reference — ETA 11/24.
- Marissa: follow up on procurement timeline and confirm any DocuSign signature needs — ETA 11/24.

Attachments mentioned: meeting recording (link pasted to shared drive) and draft SIG response (sig-response-draft.pdf).

Neha Kapoor
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
